narrativeReportMd:
# OperationDefinition R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
Breaking changes were found. Artifact identity is stable and no local R4 elements were removed, but R6 tightens required bindings and local constraints enough that some R4-valid OperationDefinitions become invalid.

## Main migration themes
Key themes are required binding changes for parameter/resource codes, hard named-query constraints, stricter parameter cardinality values, R6-only operation semantics, and semantic text changes affecting runtime discovery and governance metadata.

## Follow-up analysis
Official terminology expansions, resource lifecycle mappings, and CapabilityStatement runtime analysis would improve confidence for code mappings and invocation-name behavior.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `OperationDefinition` has hard local R4-to-R6 breaks from required binding changes and new error constraints, plus R6-to-R4 risks from new operation semantics and metadata. Top concerns are `parameter.type`, `resource`, named-query shape, and `synchronicity`.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Inventory terminology-coded fields first, then validate named queries and parameter cardinality declarations, then implement explicit extension/ConceptMap handling for R6-only fields and downgraded type/resource codes.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: High confidence for structural and binding deltas from local JSON definitions. Confidence is lower for exact terminology expansion and prevalence because official expansions, narrative pages, and instance corpora were not used.

findings.title: parameter.type required binding changed from R4 all-types to R6 fhir-types

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Compared by unchanged OperationDefinition element path/id in the local StructureDefinition snapshots/differentials.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Because the binding remains required, R4 OperationDefinitions using type codes absent from R6 can become invalid; R6-only type codes are likewise not native R4 values.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve R6 computability, validation, or operation metadata expressivity.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Use a version-independent type value set or deprecated aliases for removed R4 type/resource names.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of binding `parameter.type` to the current computable FHIR type system is reasonable, and a required binding cannot both guarantee current R6 types and freely accept removed R4 names. The compatible path is therefore only partial: it reduces migration failures but weakens the meaning of a base-valid R6 operation signature.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have bound `parameter.type` to a version-independent type value set that included R4 aliases such as retired resources or renamed datatypes, possibly flagged as deprecated. That would preserve many R4-valid definitions, but clients would need alias resolution and could see indefinitely accumulating same-concept type representations.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve more R4 OperationDefinitions but would let base R6 validators accept obsolete or non-implementable type names.

evidence.detail: Local comparison found removed R4 type codes and added R6 type codes.

examples.examplesMd: Fragments focus on the changed required binding.

findings.narrativeMd: Because the binding remains required, R4 OperationDefinitions using type codes absent from R6 can become invalid; R6-only type codes are likewise not native R4 values.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid occurs when `parameter.type` contains a removed R4 code such as `SimpleQuantity` or `TestScript`. R6-to-R4 fails for new codes such as `CodeableReference` or `integer64`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory every `parameter.type`; map removed R4 codes to R6 successors with a ConceptMap or manual review, and preserve R6-only codes through extensions or reject downgrade.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Legacy aliases or a version-independent type value set would have reduced breaks, but would keep obsolete names in R6 base validation.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `OperationDefinition.parameter.type` still has a required binding, but the bound universe moved from R4 `all-types` to R6 `fhir-types`. That means an R4 OperationDefinition using a retired or renamed type code such as `SimpleQuantity`, `TestScript`, or `ChargeItem` can fail R6 validation, and R6-only type codes cannot be represented cleanly in R4. The break is real for validators and generated operation signatures, but the element is meant to describe implementable parameter types in the current FHIR version; keeping obsolete type names base-valid would make R6 operation contracts less computable.
keyEvidence: R4 OperationDefinition.parameter.type binding is required to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/all-types|4.0.1.
R6 OperationDefinition.parameter.type binding is required to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/fhir-types|6.0.0-ballot4.
Local code comparison found 47 R4 all-types codes absent from R6 fhir-types and 37 R6 fhir-types codes absent from R4 all-types.
freshReview.fmmEffect: OperationDefinition is R4 FMM 5 and normative, so a required-binding break needs strong justification. That raised the concern, but the current-version type-system goal is strong enough that the break looks proportionate.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4-valid parameter type codes outside R6 fhir-types become invalid; there is also R6-to-R4 loss for new R6 type codes.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could have used a version-independent type value set or deprecated aliases. That would preserve more R4 definitions, but it would also require R6 validators and code generators to accept type names that are not native R6 parameter types.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: I agree this is a hard required-binding break with downgrade risk, but I would not treat the less-breaking alternative as clearly available because accepting old type names weakens R6 computability.

findings.title: resource required binding omits several R4 resource codes

oldState.summary: R4 binding was required to resource-types|4.0.1.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 binding was required to resource-types|4.0.1.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Compared by unchanged OperationDefinition element path/id in the local StructureDefinition snapshots/differentials.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A required binding makes OperationDefinitions scoped to omitted R4 resources fail R6 validation, while R6 can name resources/interfaces R4 does not know.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve R6 computability, validation, or operation metadata expressivity.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Include all R4 resource-type codes in the R6 version-independent resource value set as deprecated old types.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is version-independent resource scoping, not merely current-R6 resource scoping. Because R6 already uses a version-independent value set plus an old-types code system, omitting some R4 resource codes appears more breaking than necessary for that goal.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The base R6 value set could have included every R4 `resource-types` code, marking removed resources as retired or legacy. Validators would still distinguish current from old resources through metadata or UI filtering, while R4 OperationDefinitions scoped to those resources would remain valid.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Adds lifecycle clutter and requires deprecation metadata, but follows the existing old-types pattern and preserves old scopes.

evidence.detail: Several R4 resource codes were not found after resolving local R6 includes.

examples.examplesMd: `ChargeItem` is illustrative of an R4 resource code not accepted by the resolved local R6 value set.

findings.narrativeMd: A required binding makes OperationDefinitions scoped to omitted R4 resources fail R6 validation, while R6 can name resources/interfaces R4 does not know.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with `resource: ["ChargeItem"]` or another omitted code can be invalid in R6. R6 values such as `ActorDefinition` are not R4 resource-type codes.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map removed resource scopes to R6 successor resources or retired-operation policy. Do not silently drop scopes because that changes where an operation appears callable.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Including retired R4 resource names in the R6 value set would have been more compatible but would complicate the R6 resource taxonomy.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `OperationDefinition.resource` remains required-bound, but R6 changes the value set to a version-independent resource-type set that still omits 19 R4 resource codes. An operation scoped to an R4 resource such as `GraphDefinition`, `MedicationKnowledge`, or `TestScript` can therefore be structurally invalid in R6 even though the R6 value set already has an old-types mechanism. Because this path controls where an operation is exposed, silently dropping or remapping scopes can change runtime behavior.
keyEvidence: R4 OperationDefinition.resource binding is required to resource-types|4.0.1.
R6 OperationDefinition.resource binding is required to version-independent-all-resource-types|6.0.0-ballot4.

Local resolution of R6 all-resource-types plus fhir-old-types still excludes 19 R4 resource codes including ChargeItem, ClinicalImpression, GraphDefinition, MedicationKnowledge, MolecularSequence, TestScript, and VerificationResult.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 5/normative status strongly raises the compatibility burden because this is a hard validation break on a central operation-discovery path.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4-valid resource scope codes missing from the R6 required value set become invalid; R6-to-R4 loss also exists for R6-only resource/interface codes.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A plausible low-cost base design exists: include all R4 resource codes in the version-independent set as retired or old types. That adds lifecycle clutter, but it matches the apparent goal of version-independent resource naming and avoids invalidating old operation scopes.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the current report correctly identified a hard break and a credible less-breaking base design.

findings.title: R6 adds hard shape constraints for named queries

oldState.summary: R4 had no local root error constraints enforcing named-query shape.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 had no local root error constraints enforcing named-query shape.

newState.summary: R6 adds opd-5, opd-6, and opd-7 for query OperationDefinitions.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 adds opd-5, opd-6, and opd-7 for query OperationDefinitions.

facts.newValue: query output must be one result Bundle parameter

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Compared by unchanged OperationDefinition element path/id in the local StructureDefinition snapshots/differentials.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R6 error constraints reject named query definitions that R4 allowed, including instance-level queries, inputs without searchType, and outputs not represented as a single `result` Bundle.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve R6 computability, validation, or operation metadata expressivity.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Make the new named-query shape rules warnings or enforce them only in an R6 named-query profile.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The constraints make named queries computable and predictable: no instance-level queries, input search types are explicit, and output is a single `result` Bundle. A warning/profile approach would be less disruptive but would not provide the same base interoperability guarantee.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could have kept R4 query shapes base-valid and introduced `opd-5` through `opd-7` as warnings or as conformance requirements in an R6 profile. That alternative is incomplete because generic R6 consumers could still encounter base-valid query definitions that do not have the standardized shape.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves unusual R4 queries but prevents base R6 clients from relying on uniform query shape.

evidence.detail: R6 adds the query constraints as errors.
R4 lacks these query-shape error constraints.

examples.examplesMd: This fragment violates R6 opd-5 and opd-6.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 error constraints reject named query definitions that R4 allowed, including instance-level queries, inputs without searchType, and outputs not represented as a single `result` Bundle.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is an old-valid/new-invalid validator break driven by new error constraints on the root element.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For every `kind=query`, set `instance=false`, add `searchType` to all input parameters, and model output as exactly one `result` parameter of type `Bundle`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Warning-first constraints or a named-query profile would have been less disruptive but would not guarantee base R6 query interoperability.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds error-level named-query invariants: queries cannot be instance-level, input parameters need `searchType`, and output must be a single `result` Bundle parameter. These can reject query OperationDefinitions that were structurally allowed in R4. The affected cases are unusual or under-specified query shapes, and the R6 constraints make named queries predictable for generic clients.
keyEvidence: R4 root OperationDefinition constraints do not include opd-5, opd-6, or opd-7.
R6 root OperationDefinition constraints include opd-5 `(kind = 'query') implies (instance = false)`, opd-6 requiring input searchType for queries, and opd-7 requiring one output `result` Bundle.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 5/normative status raises the burden for adding error constraints, but named-query shape is core conformance behavior and the constraints align with query interoperability.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 query definitions with instance-level use, missing input searchType, or non-standard outputs fail R6 validation.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Warnings or a named-query profile would preserve more R4 definitions, but base R6 clients could not rely on a uniform query contract. The less-breaking option only partially meets the R6 goal.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the current report's hard-break assessment and partial alternative assessment are directionally sound.

findings.title: Parameter cardinality values are now non-negative, numeric, and internally consistent

oldState.summary: R4 used `integer` for min and unconstrained `string` for max.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 used `integer` for min and unconstrained `string` for max.

newState.summary: R6 uses `unsignedInt` for min and adds opd-8 min<=max plus opd-9 numeric-or-* max.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses `unsignedInt` for min and adds opd-8 min<=max plus opd-9 numeric-or-* max.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Compared by unchanged OperationDefinition element path/id in the local StructureDefinition snapshots/differentials.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Malformed R4 definitions with negative min, non-numeric max, or min greater than max can become invalid under R6's primitive type and error constraints.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve R6 computability, validation, or operation metadata expressivity.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the R4 lexical domains and add warning-level consistency checks for negative or malformed cardinalities.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of non-negative, numeric, internally consistent parameter cardinalities is fundamental to executable operation metadata. The affected R4-valid cases are malformed or impossible cardinality declarations, so enforcing the rule as a base error is reasonable despite the validation break.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A warning-only design could preserve R4 instances with negative `min`, non-numeric `max`, or `min > max`, but that would only partially meet the R6 goal. Implementers would still need to reject or special-case base-valid OperationDefinitions whose parameter cardinality is not meaningful.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids rejecting malformed legacy data but leaves base-valid R6 operation contracts that cannot be implemented reliably.

evidence.detail: R6 adds min/max consistency and max lexical constraints.

examples.examplesMd: No full standalone example is included; the finding is evidenced by the StructureDefinition and terminology deltas listed above.

findings.narrativeMd: Malformed R4 definitions with negative min, non-numeric max, or min greater than max can become invalid under R6's primitive type and error constraints.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid is limited to definitions whose cardinality declaration was syntactically allowed in R4 but semantically impossible or malformed.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Scan and fix negative `min`, non-numeric `max` other than `*`, and min/max inconsistencies manually.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The stricter rules are justified for implementable operation contracts; warnings would preserve bad legacy data but reduce correctness.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 makes parameter cardinality declarations computably sane: `min` is now `unsignedInt`, `max` must be numeric or `*`, and `min` cannot exceed `max`. This rejects some R4-valid lexical forms, but those forms describe negative or impossible cardinalities rather than a meaningful operation contract.
keyEvidence: R4 OperationDefinition.parameter.min type is integer.
R6 OperationDefinition.parameter.min type is unsignedInt.
R6 adds parameter constraint opd-8 for min <= max and max constraint opd-9 requiring a number or `*`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Normative/FMM 5 status requires caution, but the rejected data patterns are malformed operation signatures, so stability concerns are softened by the correctness gain.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: negative `min`, non-numeric `max`, or `min > max` can pass R4 structure validation but fail R6.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have kept the R4 lexical domains and made the checks warnings, but that would leave base-valid operation definitions with nonsensical cardinality. The tradeoff is not attractive for executable metadata.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the current report properly treats this as a real but proportionate tightening.

findings.title: searchType is now input-only and gains R6 code resource

oldState.summary: R4 allowed searchType when the parameter type was string and bound it to nine search-param-type codes.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed searchType when the parameter type was string and bound it to nine search-param-type codes.

newState.summary: R6 adds opd-4 prohibiting searchType on output parameters and adds search-param-type code `resource`.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 adds opd-4 prohibiting searchType on output parameters and adds search-param-type code `resource`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Compared by unchanged OperationDefinition element path/id in the local StructureDefinition snapshots/differentials.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Output parameters with `searchType` can become R6-invalid, and R6 definitions using `searchType=resource` cannot validate as R4.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve R6 computability, validation, or operation metadata expressivity.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Permit output `searchType` as deprecated or warning-only while keeping it meaningful only for input/search parameters.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R4-to-R6 break is the new input-only rule; the added `resource` code is a downgrade concern rather than a forward break. Prohibiting output `searchType` is a reasonable way to make search parameter semantics precise, while a softer transition would not fully remove ambiguity.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have allowed `searchType` on output parameters with a warning or with text saying it is ignored outside input/search contexts. That preserves more R4 instances, but base R6 consumers would still need to decide whether an output `searchType` is meaningful, erroneous, or legacy noise.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves odd R4 declarations but leaves ambiguity about whether output `searchType` has operational meaning.

evidence.detail: R6 adds code resource; local comparison found no removed R4 codes.

examples.examplesMd: No full standalone example is included; the finding is evidenced by the StructureDefinition and terminology deltas listed above.

findings.narrativeMd: Output parameters with `searchType` can become R6-invalid, and R6 definitions using `searchType=resource` cannot validate as R4.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 break is from the new error constraint. R6-to-R4 break is from the new required-binding code.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Remove `searchType` from output parameters or move the explanation into documentation; preserve R6 `resource` searchType with an extension or reject downgrade.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Deprecating output searchType before making it an error would have been less disruptive but less precise.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 forbids `searchType` on output parameters and adds the `resource` search-param-type code. The forward break is limited to output parameters carrying search semantics, which were already conceptually tied to input/search behavior. The added `resource` code is mainly a downgrade/enumeration issue.
keyEvidence: R4 OperationDefinition.parameter has no input-only searchType constraint.
R6 OperationDefinition.parameter includes error constraint opd-4 `(use = 'out') implies searchType.empty()`.
Local search-param-type comparison shows R6 adds `resource` and removes no R4 codes.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 5/normative status raises the bar for an error-level constraint, but the constraint removes an ambiguous output-parameter use rather than changing ordinary input search parameters.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: output parameters with searchType become invalid; R6-to-R4 loss exists for `searchType=resource`.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A warning-only transition would preserve odd R4 output declarations, but R6 consumers would still need to decide whether such output search metadata is meaningful. The stricter base rule is defensible.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the reported mechanism is real, though the practical forward break is narrow.

findings.title: binding.strength adds R6-only code descriptive

oldState.summary: R4 required binding-strength allowed required, extensible, preferred, and example.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 required binding-strength allowed required, extensible, preferred, and example.

newState.summary: R6 required binding-strength also allows descriptive.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 required binding-strength also allows descriptive.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Compared by unchanged OperationDefinition element path/id in the local StructureDefinition snapshots/differentials.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4-to-R6 is safe for existing codes, but R6 `strength=descriptive` is not in the R4 required value set and will break R4 validators/enums.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve R6 computability, validation, or operation metadata expressivity.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: adding `descriptive` widens the R6 code set and preserves R4-valid strength codes.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: This is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design change because all R4 binding-strength codes remain valid. The R6 goal of adding an explicit `descriptive` strength is reasonable; the compatibility issue is only for R6-to-R4 representation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No R4-preserving alternative is needed for forward compatibility. An extension-only representation would reduce R6 discoverability and would address downgrade compatibility rather than avoiding an R4-to-R6 break.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4 downgrade extensions or mappings are migration mitigations, not less-breaking base R6 alternatives.

examples.examplesMd: No full standalone example is included; the finding is evidenced by the StructureDefinition and terminology deltas listed above.

findings.narrativeMd: R4-to-R6 is safe for existing codes, but R6 `strength=descriptive` is not in the R4 required value set and will break R4 validators/enums.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No old-valid/new-invalid break was found; this is an R6-valid/not-R4-representable code addition.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: On downgrade, preserve `descriptive` in an extension or reject conversion; do not silently map it to `example` or `preferred`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: An extension-only design would preserve R4 enums but make R6 binding semantics less discoverable.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds the `descriptive` binding-strength code without removing any R4 codes. Existing R4 OperationDefinitions using `required`, `extensible`, `preferred`, or `example` remain valid on this path. The only issue is reverse conversion or old generated enums encountering an R6-only value.
keyEvidence: R4 binding-strength codes are required, extensible, preferred, and example.
R6 binding-strength keeps all R4 codes and adds descriptive.
OperationDefinition.parameter.binding.strength remains required-bound in both versions.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Normative/FMM 5 status does not turn a pure code-set widening into a forward compatibility problem.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 `descriptive` is not an R4 binding-strength code, but no R4-valid code is invalidated.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed for R4-to-R6 compatibility. Using only an extension for `descriptive` would optimize downgrade at the cost of weaker R6 terminology semantics.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree: the existing report treated the downgrade enum issue as medium impact, but for a fresh R4-to-R6 review this is a widening change with no old-valid/new-invalid break.

findings.title: R6 adds synchronicity invocation semantics

oldState.summary: R4 had no native synchronicity element.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 had no native synchronicity element.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional 0..1 code `synchronicity` bound to synchronous, asynchronous, or either.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 adds optional 0..1 code `synchronicity` bound to synchronous, asynchronous, or either.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Compared by unchanged OperationDefinition element path/id in the local StructureDefinition snapshots/differentials.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R6 can now state required sync/async invocation behavior. Losing this on downgrade can cause clients to call an operation using the wrong interaction pattern.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve R6 computability, validation, or operation metadata expressivity.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: `synchronicity` is an optional R6 addition and does not invalidate R4 instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The new element captures clinically and operationally important sync/async invocation behavior without creating an R4-to-R6 validation break. The remaining risk is loss of information when representing R6 content in R4.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because the element is optional and additive, there is no less-breaking base design needed to preserve R4 instances. Keeping this only as an extension would make the semantics less discoverable in R6 and would mainly optimize round-trip conversion.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4 extension/backport handling is useful for downgrade, but it is not a base R6 compatibility alternative.

evidence.detail: R6 adds synchronicity with required binding.

examples.examplesMd: No full standalone example is included; the finding is evidenced by the StructureDefinition and terminology deltas listed above.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 can now state required sync/async invocation behavior. Losing this on downgrade can cause clients to call an operation using the wrong interaction pattern.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No R4 instance becomes invalid because the field is optional. R6 instances using it are not native R4 and strict R4 parsers reject the element.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Populate it from existing operation policy when upgrading. On downgrade, preserve it in an extension or external registry and test client invocation flows.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Core support is justified by runtime importance; an R4 extension would be more round-trip compatible but less discoverable.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds optional `synchronicity` to say whether an operation is synchronous, asynchronous, or supports either. Existing R4 instances are not invalidated, but an R6 OperationDefinition using this element carries invocation semantics that R4 cannot natively represent. Losing it during downgrade can make clients choose the wrong call pattern.
keyEvidence: R4 OperationDefinition has no synchronicity element.
R6 OperationDefinition.synchronicity is 0..1 code with required binding to synchronicity-control.
R6 synchronicity-control codes are synchronous, asynchronous, and either.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 5/normative status increases attention to runtime invocation semantics, but the R6 change is additive and addresses a real operation-discovery gap.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: strict R4 models have no native field for sync/async requirements; runtime/API behavior may be wrong if the information is dropped.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Keeping this as an extension only would be more round-trip friendly, but it would make important invocation behavior less visible to base R6 clients. There is no less-breaking forward design because the addition is optional.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: I agree with the runtime importance and downgrade loss, but not with treating it as a high forward-breaking concern.

findings.title: R6 adds parameter.scope for system/type/instance applicability

oldState.summary: R4 had no native parameter-level scope element.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 had no native parameter-level scope element.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional repeating `scope` bound to instance, type, and system.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 adds optional repeating `scope` bound to instance, type, and system.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Compared by unchanged OperationDefinition element path/id in the local StructureDefinition snapshots/differentials.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R6 can restrict a parameter to a particular invocation level; R4 cannot natively preserve that, so downgraded clients may expose or send parameters at the wrong level.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve R6 computability, validation, or operation metadata expressivity.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: `parameter.scope` is an optional R6 addition and preserves R4 instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding a computable parameter-level applicability scope is a reasonable R6 improvement and does not make existing R4 OperationDefinitions invalid. The compatibility concern is that R4 has no native slot for the new information.
